headline: Voyager 1 nears one-light-day distance from Earth
summary: Voyager 1, launched nearly 49 years ago and still storing data on an eight-track tape, is reported to be the first human-made object to reach a light-day from Earth, meaning a message now takes 24 hours to arrive; Tom's Hardware instead says NASA anticipates the milestone will occur on Wednesday.

claims.statement: Voyager 1 has become the first human-made object to be a light-day away from Earth.

sources.quote: Now, it’s the first human-made object to travel a light-day away from Earth.
Space robot legend Voyager 1 is now more than 1 light-day away

claims.statement: The spacecraft stores data on an eight-track tape and has stayed in contact with scientists for decades.

sources.quote: The spacecraft stores data on an eight-track tape, but it’s managed to stay in contact with scientists for decades.

claims.statement: It now takes 24 hours to send a message to Voyager 1.

sources.quote: It now takes 24 hours to send a message to Voyager 1

claims.statement: Voyager 1 launched about 49 years ago, almost half a century before this milestone.

sources.quote: Voyager 1 spacecraft crosses milestones distance of one-light day from Earth 49 years after launch
almost half a century after launch

discrepancies.explanation: Tom's Hardware says NASA anticipates Voyager 1 will reach the light-day milestone on Wednesday, while Wired and The Register report it has already reached that distance.

quotes.quote: NASA anticipates that Voyager 1 will be the first human-made object to reach space beyond one light-day away from Earth on Wednesday.
Now, it’s the first human-made object to travel a light-day away from Earth.
